title: CarsSearch request results
description: Schema for Requests/<request_id>/results.json — one entry per car model found for that request, with the real for-sale offerings located for it. Prices are stored as integers so budget maths and UI sorting are trivial; country is an EU/EEA-restricted enum so the 'no non-EU prices' rule is enforced by schema rather than by prompt.

generated.description: ISO-8601 date or timestamp of the last write.

specs_disclaimer.description: Confidence caveat for spec fields that were not individually verified per model.

migration.description: Present only on results.json files produced by a one-shot migration of an earlier dataset. Records exactly what was carried over and what was dropped, so the losses are counted rather than silent.

model.description: One car model found for this request. The spec fields (model_variant, roof_removable, roof_mechanism, engine, fuel_or_charge_consumption, tank_or_battery_size, doors, tax, import_tax, photo) are OPTIONAL: they come from a model's spec page, and a producer that only reads listing search results cannot source them. Such a producer must omit them entirely rather than write a placeholder — a 'tbd' tax written by something that never consulted a tax table reads as a researched unknown when it is really an unasked question, which is the same class of fabrication the offering firewall exists to prevent. Consumers must therefore treat every spec field as possibly absent; docs/app.js renders a blank cell. The identifying, provenance and offering fields below stay required, because anything producing a model row at all can answer them.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique within this request. Rows are replaced wholesale by id, which is what makes a re-done model idempotent.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer as stated by the source material. brand_name is the checklist's canonical name; the two can differ (e.g. 'Bentley (Mulliner)' vs 'Bentley').

group_id.description: Config/brands.json group this model's brand belongs to; null when the brand is not on the checklist.

brand_id.description: Config/brands.json brand id; null when the manufacturer is not on the checklist.

tier.description: Price-derived market tier. Pure function of average_budget_eur plus the sold-out/bespoke and trim-spread exceptions; never hand-picked against the number.

model_variant.description: Generation / variant / trim detail and production-status notes.

first_year.description: First model year of this generation/variant, when known.

average_budget_eur.description: round(mean(offerings.price_eur)) where offerings exist; otherwise a stated estimate; null when unpriced.

roof_mechanism.description: Whether opening/removing the roof is powered or manual (free text). Renamed from the legacy roof_automated_process.

doors.description: Not pinned to 2 — requests are no longer roadster-only. Minimum 0, not 1: the Morgan Super 3 is an open three-wheeler with no doors at all, so 0 is a sourced fact and a floor of 1 rejected it. Negative is still refused, which is the part that was doing the work.

source_url.description: The page the image was taken from; null when provenance was not recorded.

search_status.description: completed_insufficient_sources means fewer than 5 surviving offerings or fewer than 2 distinct source domains — written honestly rather than padded.

search_status_note.description: Why the status is what it is (e.g. the legacy status this was migrated from).

offering_search_log.description: One entry per attempted round of the offerings ladder, so the site can show WHY a model has few offerings.

gearbox.description: Transmission type, e.g. '8-speed automatic (torque converter)', '7-speed dual-clutch', '6-speed manual', 'single-speed reduction gear'. If both manual and automatic are offered, say so. Written only when actually sourced; absent -- never null -- when it was not.

spec_source.description: Where this row's spec fields came from. Present only when they were filled by the enrichment step; absent on rows whose specs were hand-researched or never filled. A spec claim with no page behind it is discarded rather than written, so this object existing is the assertion that a page was read.

url.description: The page the values were read from.

method.description: How the page was reached. An enum so a future method is a visible change.

url.description: Must be a URL the browser actually visited — the hallucination firewall drops anything else.

source_domain.description: Registrable host of url, lowercased, without 'www.'.

location.description: City/region as displayed by the source; null when the source shows none.

price_eur.description: Asking price in EUR. Must be substring-present in the fetched page text or the offering is dropped.

price_display.description: Price exactly as displayed on the source page.

found_in_round.description: Which ladder round surfaced it; null for migrated data that predates the ladder.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the fetch; null for migrated data.

year.description: Model year as the listing card published it; null when the card showed none (a brand-new car has no first registration) or when it could not be read. Optional, and null-when-unknown rather than omitted-when-unknown, because this is the field a not_older_than request is about: publishing it is what makes that filter auditable from this file instead of only from a live re-run.

mileage.description: Odometer reading exactly as displayed by the source, units included ('123.990 km'). A string because the sources' formatting varies and reparsing it into a number here would invent precision.

fuel.description: Fuel type as the source labels it, in the source's own language ('Diesel', 'Hibrido'). Not normalised to an enum: a mapping would have to guess at labels that vary per market.

colour.description: Exterior colour of THIS car exactly as the advert states it. Null if the advert does not state one -- never infer a colour from a photo description or from the model. Written only when actually sourced; absent -- never null -- when it was not.

condition_notes.description: Any defect, damage, accident history, outstanding repair or warning the advert itself states about THIS car, quoted or closely paraphrased. Null if the advert states none. Null means the advert was silent -- it does NOT mean the car is undamaged, so never write 'no problems', 'good condition' or any other reassurance here. Written only when actually sourced; absent -- never null -- when it was not.

enrichment.description: Outcome of re-reading this listing's own page for the per-car fields. 'listing_gone' means the advert 404'd -- it sold, which is ordinary and not an error. 'not_stated' means the page was read and stated none of them. Absent means the offering predates enrichment.

url.description: The exact URL fetched for this round.

found.description: Cards parsed off the page. Equals new + duplicates.

new.description: Not seen in any earlier round or from any earlier source.

duplicates.description: Already seen in an earlier round — the progressive-exclusion counter.

dropped.description: A SUBSET OF new: those that were fetched, examined and then rejected by the firewall (unvisited URL, price not in page text, non-EU/EEA country, title does not mention the searched model, listed year older than the request allows). Not a fourth disjoint bucket — do not expect new + duplicates + dropped to equal found. A producer that verifies only the first N new cards per source leaves the remainder never examined, so new - dropped overstates how many were actually kept; firewall_kept in the brand's diagnostics is the number that were.

error.description: Timeout/block/parse failure for this round; the ladder continues to the next rung regardless.

tax_value.description: Typed from the start so 'TBD' never has to migrate from string to number later.

basis.description: How the value was determined; empty string while status is tbd.

body_type.description: Kept identical to request.schema.json's body_type enum — tools/verify.py asserts the two lists match.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2, restricted to EU/EEA. A listing outside this set is dropped by the firewall, not stored.
